answer:
Tribes that had originated in the area of the Linear Pottery (LBK) culture—most notably the Vandals, the Alans and the Suebi—made a major incursion into the Western Roman Empire at the very end of the year **406 AD**.  

According to the widely‑cited account of the “Crossing of the Rhine” (Wikipedia, *Crossing of the Rhine*), the invasion by these mixed Germanic and Sarmatian groups is traditionally dated to **31 December 406 AD** (the last day of the year). The event is considered a key turning point in the decline of the Western Roman Empire.  

Thus, the tribes from the Linear Pottery culture zone entered Roman territory at the end of **406 A.D.**.

The **crossing of the Rhine** by a mixed group of Germanic and [Sarmatian] tribes which included [Vandals], [Alans] and [Suebi] is traditionally considered to have occurred on 31 December 406.[[1]] The crossing transgressed one of the Late [Roman Empire]'s most secure _[limes] "Limes (Roman Empire)")_ or boundaries; as such, it has been considered a climactic moment in the [decline of the empire]. It initiated a wave of destruction of Roman cities and the collapse of Roman civic order in northern [Gaul]. That, in turn, occasioned the rise of three usurpers in succession in the province of [Britannia]. Therefore, the crossing of the [Rhine] is a marker date in the [Migration Period] during which various [Germanic tribes] moved westward and southward from southern [Scandinavia] and northern [Germania].

Tribes that had originated in the area of the Linear Pottery (LBK) culture—most notably the Vandals, the Alans and the Suebi—made a major incursion into the Western Roman Empire at the very end of the year **406 AD**.  

According to the widely‑cited account of the “Crossing of the Rhine” (Wikipedia, *Crossing of the Rhine*), the invasion by these mixed Germanic and Sarmatian groups is traditionally dated to **31 December 406 AD** (the last day of the year). The event is considered a key turning point in the decline of the Western Roman Empire.  

Thus, the tribes from the Linear Pottery culture zone entered Roman territory at the end of **406 A.D.**.
